children: OpenAI keeps pushing back its planned initial public offering. But investors wanting to bet on the ChatGPT developer will soon have an option.

SB Energy, the infrastructure company set up by OpenAI and Japan's SoftBank Group, to build, own, and operate data centers, is looking to list. Its IPO filing could be made public as soon as this week, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Anyone looking at SB Energy as a potential investment will be implicitly making a bet that OpenAI is going to be a success. OpenAI has invested $500 million in SB Energy and received warrants worth an estimated $5.5 billion in the company, according to the Journal.

OpenAI is both a major investor in SB Energy and its key customer. SoftBank and OpenAI are the expected tenants for three SB Energy data centers that are under construction, although the company also has a fourth with no set customer. That means they likely represent the vast majority of its contracted revenue backlog of more than $400 billion.

For those trying to figure out how to value that revenue, the closest comparison is cloud-computing companies such as CoreWeave. In fact, OpenAI and SB Energy are likely to have a similar dynamic to CoreWeave and its major investor, customer, and supplier Nvidia.

CoreWeave had a revenue backlog of $104 billion as of June 30 and is valued at around $46.5 billion. SB Energy's reported contracts for nine gigawatts of computing capacity would be bigger than CoreWeave 4.2 gigawatts of contracted power.

However, CoreWeave has a more diversified customer base for its computing power and already has 51 active data centers and 1.5 gigawatts of active power. SB Energy doesn't have any data centers in operation and has 800 megawatts of computing capacity under construction.

At least SB Energy shouldn't have trouble getting access to chips. Nvidia has committed $3 billion to SB Energy through transactions tied to its IPO, including one that allows the chip maker to acquire shares at a 10% discount to the public offering price, the Journal reported.

Of course, the economics of an infrastructure provider like SB Energy and an artificial-intelligence developer like OpenAI will be very different. But it is likely to trade at least in part as a proxy for its backer, which might attract-or deter-many investors, until the real thing finally comes to market, which is expected next year.
